facts: A real two-floor smart-factory project planned phased use from roughly 5000 square metres to 10000-15000 square metres.
The mandated architecture used dual carrier links, HA perimeter firewalls, dual core switches and a separate IT/OT firewall boundary.
The request required configuration-level switching, wireless, security, cabling and operations BOMs with current manufacturer evidence.
findings: Area alone cannot determine AP quantity; wall materials, ceiling height, machinery, interference, client density and roaming paths require an active survey.
Access-switch and cabling quantities cannot be fixed before CAD drawings and the information-point schedule are reconciled.
Firewall selection must use threat-protection throughput with IPS, antimalware and application identification enabled, not stateful throughput.
Buying final-scale core, firewall and controller capacity while phasing AP, access-port and endpoint licenses avoids replacing phase-one platforms.
rule_changes: Require official lifecycle/orderability evidence for every named model.
Require AP PoE calculations using maximum device draw plus 20 percent reserve.
Separate confirmed platform choices from survey-dependent quantities.
limitations: No supplier quotations, award value, settlement value or operational measurements were available at the time of review.
This case validates requirements handling and uncertainty disclosure; it does not validate final market-price accuracy.
Factory identity, exact process names and location details are removed or generalized.
